data.title: Watcher ticks cannot do web research: WebFetch/WebSearch denied by headless --allowedTools grant set

data.body:
Discovered during watcher tick watcher:96123 (2026-09-01), while researcher-nadia answered a board DM (#DM 13 msg 381) asking for D1's main competitors.

SYMPTOM: every WebFetch call from the tick sub-agent was permission-denied. Nadia attempted Bonsai, Plutio, and FreshBooks pricing pages; all three denied. She correctly refused to fabricate URLs or substitute aggregator links, and instead relabelled every source in docs/strategy/12-d1-competitive-landscape.md as inherited-unverified from the 2026-08-30 evidence file. Net effect: the board asked to 'look into' competitors and received a record with ZERO clickable sources, because the citation chain terminates in another internal doc (docs/strategy/evidence/competitive-lanes.md) that also has no URLs.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, needs confirming): AS-21 made the watcher pass permission grants explicitly via --allowedTools/--disallowedTools in tickArgv() (apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs), because project-scope .claude/settings.json is inert for headless 'claude -p' children. That grant set was built for the Bash/lattice/git write path and evidently does not include WebFetch or WebSearch. So headless ticks are silently incapable of any external research.

WHY IT MATTERS: market and competitive research is a standing company function (two research ICs on staff, an evidence-template process, docs/strategy/evidence/*). Today it only works in live /loop sessions, and fails in exactly the message-triggered ticks that are supposed to be the board's primary interface. It fails QUIETLY -- the tick still produces a plausible-looking document, just one built entirely from stale inherited facts. That is the dangerous shape: a competitive record whose prices silently age out while reading as current.

SCOPE: add WebFetch/WebSearch to the tick grant set in tickArgv() and verify a watcher-fired tick can actually retrieve an external page. Preserve the existing git push --force deny rules (the AS-21 constraint -- do not regress to bypassPermissions). Consider whether any egress restriction is wanted on WebFetch domains; that is a board-facing judgment call if so.

FOLLOW-ON (not this task): once ticks can fetch, docs/strategy/12-d1-competitive-landscape.md and docs/strategy/evidence/competitive-lanes.md both need a pass to attach real vendor-pricing URLs and re-verify the price points, which are currently 2026-08-30 vintage and unverified.

NEEDS HUMAN (cto-owen, tick watcher:12263 loop 3 tick 20). Root cause confirmed by observation, not argument: a WebFetch of https://example.com/ from inside this watcher-fired tick returned 'requested permissions to use WebFetch, but you haven't granted it yet'. The watcher code is already right — tickArgv() (apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs) forwards .claude/settings.json's allow list verbatim as --allowedTools (AS-21) — and that list has no WebFetch or WebSearch entry. The whole fix is two lines in .claude/settings.json permissions.allow: "WebFetch" and "WebSearch". That file is metawork-layer plumbing employees do not edit (AS-103 record), so this is the board's edit, not a lane. Judgment call bundled in: the task asked whether an egress restriction on WebFetch domains is wanted; CTO recommendation is none — the tool is read-only, the research ICs need arbitrary vendor and pricing sites, and the deny list (force-push, gh pr merge) is untouched. If a restriction is wanted, the form is WebFetch(domain:<host>) entries instead of the bare tool. Verification once applied: the next watcher-fired tick fetches one external page and the tick report says so; then AS-55 goes to done with no code merge (no branch, no worktree). Follow-on stays as written on this record: re-verify docs/strategy/12-d1-competitive-landscape.md and evidence/competitive-lanes.md price points with real URLs.

REVIEW (qa-priya, inside watcher:12263 loop 3 tick 21). Change under review: f6a5177, .claude/settings.json permissions.allow += "WebFetch", "WebSearch". No branch, no diff.

FINDINGS (2, neither blocks):
F1. The argv is no longer the only transport, and the code/README say it is. This tick's live child (pid 75224, started 21:31:34Z, before the 21:39Z edit) was spawned with an --allowedTools set that does NOT contain WebFetch/WebSearch (verified via ps). Yet WebFetch https://example.com/ returned title 'Example Domain' + first sentence, and WebSearch 'example.com IANA reserved domain' returned 9 result links (iana.org first). Explanation with evidence: ~/.claude.json has hasTrustDialogAccepted:true for this repo, and the 'Ignoring N permissions.allow entries … not trusted' line last appears in tick logs dated 2026-08-31 — none since. So project settings.json now loads (and re-loads) for headless children directly; the AS-21 argv is a belt. Comments at advance-watcher.mjs:343-354, 2684-2685 and watch/README.md:645-647 describe the pre-trust world. Doc residual, backlog, not a v1 blocker. Falsifier: an 'Ignoring' line in any post-08-31 tick log.
F2. The red is the CTO's tick-20 observation ('requested permissions to use WebFetch, but you haven't granted it yet'), not mine; I did not revert a metawork file inside a live tick to reproduce it. Stated, not hidden.

FLOOR CHECK (Owen's 3 items):
1. Mechanism: fire() -> loadPermissionRules(paths.settings) -> tickArgv() -> --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, re-read per fire. Via argv the change reaches the NEXT tick; via loaded settings it reached this already-running one (observed). PASS.
2. Behaviour: WebFetch success, WebSearch success, texts above. PASS.
3. Probe: deny list identical before/after (4 entries: force-push x3, gh pr merge); allow 14->16, only the two additions, no other entry altered, file has only 'permissions' key; watcher.test.js argv pin 73/73 green. Egress question: CTO recommended no domain restriction; the board applied bare tools, which is that decision made — disposed of, no open decision. Read-only tools; no spend, no GitHub/DO write path. PASS.

VERDICT: PASS. No inline fixes made. Follow-on stays as written (re-verify competitive-landscape price points with real URLs).

DONE (cto-owen, tick watcher:12263 loop 3 tick 21). Board applied the two allow-list lines (f6a5177) and moved the task to review from the dashboard; Priya's review (Opus after a Fable 429) recorded PASS — WebFetch and WebSearch both succeeded from inside this watcher-fired tick, deny list byte-identical, only the two additions on the allow side, egress question disposed of by the board applying the bare tools. No branch, no worktree, no merge. Triage: Priya's finding 1 (advance-watcher.mjs:343-354, 2684-2685 and watch/README.md:645-647 describe the argv as the only transport; project settings now also load directly for headless children since the trust dialog was accepted) is a prose residual, stays on this record, folds into the next task touching that file. Follow-on stays as written: re-verify docs/strategy/12-d1-competitive-landscape.md and evidence/competitive-lanes.md price points with real URLs — that is research, not a Lattice task.
